उत्तरी और मध्य वियतनाम में भीषण गर्मी की लहर छाई हुई है।
एसकेडीएस - 2 सितंबर को राष्ट्रीय दिवस की छुट्टी के शेष दिनों में, वियतनाम के उत्तरी और मध्य क्षेत्रों में गर्म मौसम रहेगा और तापमान 35 डिग्री सेल्सियस से अधिक रहेगा।
Báo Sức khỏe và Đời sống•31/08/2026
राष्ट्रीय मौसम विज्ञान और जल विज्ञान पूर्वानुमान केंद्र के अनुसार, 31 अगस्त को उत्तरी वियतनाम के पहाड़ी और मध्यभूमि क्षेत्रों में स्थानीय स्तर पर भीषण गर्मी की लहरें चलीं, जहां दोपहर 1 बजे कुछ स्थानों पर तापमान 35 डिग्री सेल्सियस से अधिक हो गया।
1 सितंबर को उत्तरी क्षेत्र ( डिएन बिएन , लाई चाऊ और सोन ला को छोड़कर) में भीषण गर्मी पड़ी, कुछ इलाकों में तो भीषण गर्मी का प्रकोप रहा। अधिकतम तापमान आमतौर पर 35-37 डिग्री सेल्सियस रहा, कुछ स्थानों पर तो यह 37 डिग्री सेल्सियस से भी अधिक था; न्यूनतम सापेक्ष आर्द्रता आमतौर पर 45-50% थी। 2 सितंबर को गर्मी धीरे-धीरे कम होने लगी।
2 सितंबर को, थान्ह होआ से दा नांग शहर तक और क्वांग न्गाई प्रांत के पूर्वी हिस्से में भीषण गर्मी पड़ी, कुछ इलाकों में तो भीषण गर्मी का प्रकोप रहा। अधिकतम तापमान आमतौर पर 35-37 डिग्री सेल्सियस रहा, कुछ जगहों पर यह 37 डिग्री सेल्सियस से भी अधिक था; न्यूनतम सापेक्ष आर्द्रता आमतौर पर 50-55% थी। लू की चेतावनी: मध्य क्षेत्र में लू 3-4 सितंबर तक जारी रहने की संभावना है। लू के खतरे का स्तर: स्तर 1।
आपको यह भी पसंद आ सकता है
तीव्र गर्मी और कम आर्द्रता के संयुक्त प्रभाव से, बिजली की बढ़ती मांग के कारण आवासीय क्षेत्रों में विस्फोट और आग लगने का खतरा है। इसके अलावा, लंबे समय तक उच्च तापमान के संपर्क में रहने से निर्जलीकरण हो सकता है।
कृपया ध्यान दें कि लू की रिपोर्टों में तापमान का पूर्वानुमान और बाहर का वास्तविक तापमान 1-3 डिग्री या उससे भी अधिक भिन्न हो सकता है, जो कंक्रीट या डामर जैसी सतहों की स्थिति पर निर्भर करता है।
1 से 9 सितंबर तक हनोई का मौसम: हनोई में मौसम अधिकतर बादल छाए रहेंगे और बारिश नहीं होगी। दिन में धूप खिली रहेगी और अधिकतम तापमान आमतौर पर 34-35 डिग्री सेल्सियस के बीच रहेगा। विशेष रूप से, 1 सितंबर को न्यूनतम तापमान 27 डिग्री सेल्सियस और अधिकतम तापमान 35 डिग्री सेल्सियस रहेगा। 2 सितंबर को तापमान 26-34 डिग्री सेल्सियस के बीच रहेगा।
3 से 5 सितंबर तक न्यूनतम तापमान आमतौर पर 26-27 डिग्री सेल्सियस और अधिकतम तापमान 34-35 डिग्री सेल्सियस रहेगा। 6 से 7 सितंबर को अधिकतम तापमान लगभग 35 डिग्री सेल्सियस और न्यूनतम तापमान 27 डिग्री सेल्सियस रहेगा।
आपको यह भी पसंद आ सकता है
8-9 सितंबर को मौसम में बादल छाए रहेंगे, बारिश नहीं होगी, न्यूनतम तापमान 27 डिग्री सेल्सियस और अधिकतम तापमान लगभग 34 डिग्री सेल्सियस रहेगा।
कुल मिलाकर, अगले 10 दिनों तक हनोई में हल्की बारिश होगी, धूप खिली रहेगी और अधिकतम तापमान 34-35 डिग्री सेल्सियस के बीच रहेगा। लोगों को बाहरी गतिविधियों में भाग लेते समय, विशेषकर दोपहर और दोपहर के शुरुआती घंटों में, अपने स्वास्थ्य की सुरक्षा के लिए सावधानी बरतनी चाहिए।

Swiss construction union calls for stronger protections against extreme heat
82% of surveyed workers do not consistently receive required breaks at 91.4F, Unia says
Seyma Erkul Dayanc
31 August 2026•Update: 31 August 2026
ISTANBUL
Switzerland’s Unia trade union on Monday called for stronger heat protections for construction workers after a survey found that most workers do not consistently receive the required breaks during heat waves.
Unia surveyed 984 construction workers across Switzerland in July and found that only 18% consistently received the 15-minute hourly break required when temperatures reach 33C (91.4F). Some 67% said they never received such breaks, while 15% received them only sometimes, according to Swissinfo.
The survey also found that more than two-thirds of workers said their working hours were not adjusted to avoid the hottest part of the day.
Some 15% said they had experienced a heat-related health incident or witnessed one involving a colleague.
“The question is not whether working in extreme heat is tiring or unpleasant: it is health and safety at work that are at stake,” Unia said.
The union called for a 33C (91.4F) threshold to be included in Switzerland’s Construction Work Ordinance, with strenuous outdoor work suspended above that threshold unless 15-minute hourly breaks in air-conditioned areas can be guaranteed.
Unia also urged authorities to increase workplace inspections and called for construction deadlines and compensation rules to be adjusted to account for work stoppages caused by extreme heat.

A shopper browses the produce aisle in a grocery store in Seoul on Aug. 18.NEWS1
The heat is changing more than what Koreans buy. It is changing when, where and how they spend.
For a parent surnamed Lee, weekends now start at 7 a.m. The family finds it difficult to go out during the hottest part of the day, so early-morning walks near their home or indoor retreats to air-conditioned places have become a weekend routine.
“We tend to stay home during the hottest part of the day or spend time at a department store or cafe,” Lee said. “I can’t wait for fall, when we can finally go outside and enjoy the cool breeze.”
Record-breaking heat waves each summer are reshaping consumers’ daily routines. People are buying more in fewer trips, while department stores and cafes are becoming places to linger for relatively little money. Spending has also shifted away from the afternoon toward mornings and evenings.
On heat wave days, supermarket transactions rose 7.3 percent compared to other days, while online shopping transactions increased 4.1 percent, an analysis by Shinhan Card released Saturdayshowed.
Shinhan Card's big data analysis lab examined a month of card spending by customers in the greater Seoul area from July 18, comparing heat wave days, when the daily high reached at least 33 degrees Celsius (91.4 degrees Fahrenheit), with days below that threshold.
Shoppers were not just buying more often. They were spending more each time. Average spending per transaction rose 5.2 percent at supermarkets and 11.6 percent online.
“Consumers showed a clear tendency to stock up by buying more at once and spending larger amounts because of the heat,” the institute said.
Department stores and cafes told a different story.
Transactions increased 1 percent at department stores and 6.5 percent at cafes on heat wave days. Yet average spending per transaction fell 5.5 percent and 3.6 percent, respectively.
The figures suggest consumers increasingly use such places as air-conditioned refuges from the heat — buying little and staying for a long time — rather than primarily as shopping destinations.
Taxi use followed a similar pattern. The number of rides rose 7.2 percent, but average spending per ride fell 1.3 percent. The heat appears to have made even short walks less appealing and boosted demand for short-distance taxi trips.
Hot weather also changed when people opened their wallets.
An analysis of spending times across 20 major business categories found that the share of purchases made between 6 a.m. and 11 a.m. was 1.24 percentage points higher on heat wave days than on other days, while the share between 3 p.m. and 6 p.m. fell 1.37 percentage points.
The shift was particularly noticeable for essential errands. The share of visits made in the morning rose 1.4 percentage points at hospitals and 1.9 percentage points at pharmacies.
Traditional markets and outlet malls, where shoppers are more exposed to the heat, saw their share of afternoon spending fall 1.4 percentage points and 2.1 percentage points, respectively.
Business picked up again after the heat eased. Between 6 p.m. and 9 p.m., the share of spending rose 1.8 percentage points at traditional markets and 1.3 percentage points at outlets.
The evening rebound was particularly pronounced among consumers aged 60 and older.
On heat wave days, the number of customers in that age group who visited large grocery stores between 6 p.m. and 9 p.m. rose 5.6 percent. Similarly, cafe visits increased 7.6 percent. Both were the largest increases of any age group.
The figures suggest older consumers, who are particularly vulnerable to extreme heat, are actively adjusting their everyday spending habits.
Senior citizens also turned to delivery apps more often, with usage of those in their 60s or older up 6.8 percent on heat wave days. Convenience store shopping also rose 6.8 percent.
In addition, ice cream and shaved ice purchases among older adult consumers jumped 32 percent on heat wave days, the largest increase of all age groups.
The hotter it got, the more spending moved from stores to screens.
Average spending per online shopping transaction surged 35.4 percent between 3 p.m. and 6 p.m. on heat wave days, compared to days without extreme heat.
Outlet malls moved in the opposite direction. Average spending per transaction declined across all time periods and fell 11.6 percent between 3 p.m. and 6 p.m.
For retailers and consumers alike, the numbers are clear: When the heat peaks, the shopping trip can wait.

30th August 2026 will be remembered as a great day for fans of professional wrestling. NXT Heatwave 2026 took place and there were 5 Matches that took place. Each one of them was good and a couple of them were incredible. This show had multiple title changes which was the theme of the day in WWE and AEW.
Let’s look at the Results for NXT Heatwave 2026
Zaria beat Wren Sinclair and Kali Armstrong for NXT North American Championship and WWE Women’s Speed Championship
The first match on the show was a triple threat match for the unified titles in the women’s division. It was Zaria who was taking on the Speed Champion Wren Sinclair and Kali Armstrong. This was a 12 minute match where all 3 women got the opportunity to shine. Zaria and Kali Armstrong were initially ignoring Wren Sinclair but Wren Sinclair came back in the match. These three women were hitting each other with Suplexes and Kali Armstrong eventually took control of the match. There was a great spot where Wren Sinclair Superplexed Zaria. To end the match, Zaria hit the F5 on Kali Armstrong to become the unified champion.
The Vanity Project beat Myles Bourne and Tavion Heights for NXT Tag Team Championship
This was the second title change of the night. This tag team match was 14 minutes of non stop action. Myles Bourne was injured on the ribs and The Vanity Project kept attacking his ribs and prevented him from tagging Tavion Heights. Tavion Heights got the hot tag and he started giving Suplexes to both men and he applied the ankle lock. Myles Bourne hit two Powerslams and then followed it up with a Neckbreaker and DDT combo. A momentary lapse in focus and The Vanity Project won the match and became new NXT Tag Team Champions.
Kelani Jordan beat Kendal Grey for NXT Women’s Championship
Women’s wrestling was the winner on 30th August 2026. There were 2 Matches throughout the night at All In and Heatwave that went 23 minutes each. This one between Kendal Grey vs Kelani Jordan was the best match of NXT Heatwave. Kelani Jordan started the match hitting an Asai MoonSault which was not enough. Kelani Jordan started attacking the injured ear of Kendal Grey and it was a test for the champion. Both these women were locked in as Kendal Grey hit Overhead and German Suplexes and Kelani Jordan hit a Northern Lights Suplex. The fans were chanting This is Awesome. Kelani Jordan jumped over Kendal Grey and smashed the announce table. Kendal Grey hit a Reverse Spanish Fly and Kelani Jordan answered it with a twisting springboard cutter. Both women hit 450 Splashes, German Suplexes. Kelani Jordan won the title by hitting her MoonSault finisher. This was professional wrestling at its very best.
Jackson Drake beat Myles Bourne for NXT North American Championship
This was the shortest match of the night and it was understandable. Myles Bourne had already competed in a match. This was a 10 minute match. Myles Bourne fought with all his heart as he brought Jackson Drake down. Jackson Drake countered it with a series of kicks to the rib section. Tavion Heights came out to even the odds but The Vanity Project proved too much. Jackson Drake hit the 450 Splash to win the NXT North American Championship. This was a surprising title change. After the match Myles Bourne turned heel in a shocking outcome.
Grayson Waller beat Zilla Fatu, Cruz Montana and Tony D Angelo for NXT Championship
This was a 21 minute barn burner for the NXT Championship. There were 4 men who were looking to be the top dog in NXT. Zilla Fatu showed his power as he started giving Samoan Drops to all his opponents. Tony D Angelo gave a Spinebuster to Zilla Fatu. Cruz Montana delivered a Suicide Dive to the outside on all 3 of his opponents. Zilla Fatu hit the Samoan Spike on the champion and nearly won but Grayson Waller stopped the referee from counting. Grayson Waller delivered an elbow drop to Zilla Fatu on top of the announce table. full_text:
As the planet gets hotter, the human body can only do so much to keep itself cool. For older adults — defined in the study as people 60 and older — the limit may arrive much sooner than previously understood.
A new study from Stanford University found older adults are far more vulnerable to extreme heat than younger people. Even if global warming is limited to 2.7 degrees above preindustrial levels, older adults are projected to be exposed to heat their bodies cannot tolerate more often than young adults would in a world warmed nearly three times as much.
Previous global projections of heat beyond what the human body can manage mostly used healthy adults in their 20s to set the baseline.
The study, published in The Lancet Planetary Health, is the first to project global exposure to “uncompensable heat stress,” a condition when the body is exposed to heat that exceeds its ability to maintain a stable core temperature, for different age groups.
“It doesn’t mean immediate death once exposed,” said Qinqin Kong, the study’s lead author and a postdoctoral scholar at Stanford University.
Instead, once the heat threshold is crossed, core body temperature will continue to rise. If the exposure to high temperatures lasts long enough, it can eventually lead to serious or lethal injury.
That distinction makes this level of heat different from familiar measures such as air temperature or the heat index because it focuses on how weather affects the body, said Eran Bendavid, a Stanford professor of medicine and study co-author.
Researchers combined climate projections and population estimates with heat-tolerance limits established through controlled laboratory experiments. In those experiments, participants are placed in environmental chambers where heat and humidity are progressively increased. At the same time, researchers monitor participants’ core temperatures to determine when they can no longer maintain thermal balance.
The research indicates the temperature at which adults 60 and older can no longer maintain a stable core temperature is roughly 8.5 to 13.5 degrees lower than it is for younger adults, depending on humidity.
There are several reasons.
Sweat glands become less effective with age, reducing one of the body’s primary mechanisms for shedding heat. Blood vessels also become less effective at dilating to move warm blood toward the skin, where that heat can escape, Kong said.
“As we age, multiple parts of our bodies’ cooling mechanisms become less effective,” Kong said.
The thirst response can also weaken with age, making dehydration more likely.
Chronic health conditions and medications common among older adults can further interfere with sweating, circulation and other mechanisms the body relies on to withstand extreme heat.
When researchers incorporated those age-specific differences into their projections, the scale of older adults’ potential exposure to heat that could damage their bodies increased dramatically.
At 2.7 degrees of global warming above preindustrial temperatures, about 22% of people 60 and older worldwide — roughly 290 million people — are projected to experience at least 180 hours per year in which environmental conditions exceed their age-specific ability to withstand heat. Younger adults would not experience a comparable level of exposure until warming approaches 7.2 degrees.
The researchers also found that every additional degree of warming could expose roughly another billion people ages 15 and older worldwide to at least 180 hours of such heat each year. At 5.4 degrees of warming, older people in some of the hardest-hit parts of South Asia and the Persian Gulf could face such conditions day and night for three consecutive months annually.
But Bendavid said the study’s central contribution isn’t necessarily the billion-person figure. Scientists already knew that more warming would expose more people to dangerous heat. What they didn’t know is how much of this burden would be borne by older people.
“The world is getting older, and the world is getting warmer. There’s going to be some confluence of these demographics and these climate conditions. It’s a perfect storm,” Bendavid said.
The effects won’t be distributed evenly. South Asia and the Arabian Peninsula are among the regions where the researchers project the most intense convergence of aging populations and uncompensable heat.
Lara Cushing, an associate professor of environmental health sciences at UCLA who was not involved with the research, called the analysis significant. She said the study illustrates a fundamental limit to society’s ability to respond to rising temperatures naturally.
“You can’t adapt your way out of every problem,” Cushing said.
Air conditioning, cooling centers and other interventions can protect people, but they do not eliminate the underlying physical limits, she said. Unless people can spend their lives in air-conditioned environments, continued warming will increasingly put people into conditions their bodies cannot tolerate.
Cushing said socioeconomic inequality is an important part of the picture. Low-income households, unhoused people and outdoor workers may have fewer resources to escape dangerous temperatures. Access to air conditioning, transportation and safe housing can determine whether two people experiencing the same weather face very different levels of actual risk.
“So much of this is about resources you have to mitigate your risk,” Cushing said.
That means older adults shouldering some of the greatest climate-related health burdens may also be among those with the fewest resources to protect themselves.
The researchers also acknowledge a limitation: The thresholds used in the model come largely from controlled experiments conducted in the United States. People who routinely live in hotter climates may be somewhat more acclimatized to heat. Researchers tested scenarios allowing higher heat-tolerance limits in warmer climates and found that doing so reduced the estimated exposure but did not change the study’s overall conclusions.
Heat can be particularly dangerous because people don’t always recognize that they are developing heat exhaustion before their condition progresses.
“It’s a silent killer,” Cushing said.
Kong said protecting an aging population will also require changes beyond individual behavior. Heat action plans should recognize that risk isn’t one-size-fits-all, he said. Communities may need earlier warnings for older adults, accessible cooling spaces and systems to reach people who may otherwise be isolated during extreme heat.
Cushing said those adaptations remain essential, but the findings also reinforce the importance of addressing the underlying cause of increasing heat exposure: continued global warming.
In the Bay Area, a growing older population is increasingly confronting rising temperatures. While coastal communities are somewhat buffered by the Pacific Ocean, inland parts of Alameda, Contra Costa and Santa Clara counties routinely experience much higher temperatures during heat waves.
She added that the age-related vulnerability identified by the study isn’t only a concern for people who are old today. Children born now will become older adults toward the end of the century, when they could experience some of the most severe effects of a climate that has continued warming throughout their lives.
“We have to think to ourselves, what kind of world are we leaving them?” she said.

The rainfall deficit in eastern Uttar Pradesh, western Uttar Pradesh and the state as a whole, which stood at 34%, 15% and 27%, respectively, at the end of July, has since improved to fall within the normal rainfall category.
The India Meteorological Department has issued orange and yellow alerts for Uttar Pradesh, forecasting continued rainfall over the next few days under the influence of a well-marked low-pressure area over the northwest Bay of Bengal and the West Bengal-North Odisha coast.
“Due to a low-pressure area over the northwest Bay of Bengal and adjoining West Bengal-North Odisha coast, along with a western disturbance in the form of a cyclonic circulation over northwest Punjab and adjoining Jammu and Kashmir, monsoon activity is likely to increase significantly over Uttar Pradesh during the next 24-48 hours. Isolated heavy to very heavy rainfall is likely over eastern and southeastern Uttar Pradesh. Subsequently, as the low-pressure area moves further, the focus of rainfall is expected to gradually shift towards southern Uttar Pradesh and the Bundelkhand region,” said Atul Kumar Singh, senior scientist at the Regional Meteorological Centre, Lucknow.
The rainfall deficit in eastern Uttar Pradesh, western Uttar Pradesh and the state as a whole, which stood at 34%, 15% and 27%, respectively, at the end of July, has since improved to fall within the normal rainfall category. As of August 30, eastern UP has a 14% deficit, while western UP has recorded 3% excess rainfall and the state overall has a 7% deficit. Rainfall between 19% surplus and 19% deficit is considered normal.
As of now, 30 districts in Uttar Pradesh have recorded deficient or large deficient rainfall, while 31 districts have received normal rainfall. Ten districts have recorded excess rainfall and four have received large excess rainfall during the monsoon season so far.
During the past 24 hours, the Baberu meteorological observatory in Banda recorded very heavy rainfall of 217.6 mm. Naraini in Banda received 98.2 mm, while Bisalpur in Pilibhit recorded 75 mm and Gonda Sadar 70.6 mm, with all three receiving heavy rainfall.
For Monday, the IMD has issued an orange alert for Chitrakoot, Prayagraj, Sonbhadra, Mirzapur, Chandauli and adjoining areas. A yellow alert for heavy to very heavy rainfall has been issued for Banda, Kaushambi, Fatehpur, Pratapgarh, Varanasi, Sant Ravidas Nagar, Jaunpur, Bahraich, Lakhimpur Kheri, Rampur, Bareilly, Pilibhit, Shahjahanpur and adjoining areas, the weatherman said.
